$comment: ★ EVERY SPELLING C GIVES THE `long` AND `long long` INTEGER SUFFIXES, MIXED CASE INCLUDED (P68 round 11, D-C-MIXED-CASE-INTEGER-SUFFIXES-REFUSED). C 6.4.4.1 builds an integer-suffix from an unsigned-suffix (`u`/`U`) and a long-suffix (`l`/`L`) or long-long-suffix (`ll`/`LL`) in either order, each part cased on its own: 22 spellings. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c11 -pedantic-errors` and their default modes, -O0/-O2), aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc under qemu, mingw-w64 gcc and MSVC 19.51 (`/std:c17`, `/std:clatest`, /Od and /O2) run this file to 42. DSS refused `uL`, `Ul`, `lU`, `Lu`, `uLL`, `Ull`, `llU` and `LLu` with P_MalformedNumber (51 diagnostics on this file, the phase-4 `#error` among them), because `src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json` listed only the single-case combinations — in `numberStyle.integerSuffixes` and in the 6.4.4.1 ladder's `suffixes` groups, which the loader requires to agree. What each value proves, by the exit code: 1-6 the single spellings, 7-14 the eight `unsigned long` spellings, 15-22 the eight `unsigned long long` ones — each by its TYPE (`_Generic`) and its value against a `volatile`; 23-26 the `unsigned long` ladder's next rung at 2^36 - 1, decimal and hexadecimal (`unsigned long` on LP64, `unsigned long long` on LLP64); 27-28 the largest `unsigned long long`. The `#if` blocks read the same spellings in phase 4 (C 6.10.1p4): the value, and that a `u` makes the literal unsigned. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: drop one spelling from both lists and this file does not compile; drop it from one list only and the loader refuses the language document. The `release` arm pins the same file through the shipped release pipeline.
